items.title: New York Fed's Williams says yield surge due to strong economic prospects
items.summary: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said Wednesday that the recent surge in Treasury yields is the product of a strong economy , not market dysfunction.

items.title: Berkshire CEO Greg Abel says Japanese bond yields not a challenge for trading houses right now
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's CEO Greg Abel said that rising yields in Japan isn't impacting the major trading houses in the country the holding company has stakes in.

items.title: Nepal’s mountain tourism industry faces ‘serious warning’ after Himalayan flood disaster
items.summary: Nepal's renowned adventure tourism industry faces a sobering reality check, according to local mountain tourist associations and hostel owners, following devastating flooding on Nepal's border with China.

items.title: Hugging Face's new duck robot is selling fast. A Chinese chip powers it
items.summary: BEIJING — A popular new programmable personal robot from a French-American company is powered by a chip from Shanghai-listed Rockchip which in turn uses British company ARM's tech, reflecting how intertwined global tech supply chains remain.

items.title: Prediction market traders think job creation rebounded in August
items.summary: After a disappointing July payrolls report that showed the economy lost jobs that month, traders on prediction market platforms think August will show a rebound in hiring, though potentially not as strong as economists think.

items.title: China's Xi builds diplomatic clout with multiple state visits ahead of Trump summit
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to make rare state visits to Egypt and, likely India, before his expected trip to the U.S. in late September.

items.title: Private payrolls rose by 38,000 in August, less than expected, ADP reports
items.summary: Private U.S. companies added jobs at a slightly slower-than-expected pace in August, with gains concentrated heavily in healthcare and a few other industries, ADP reported Wednesday.

HPE follows in Dell’s footsteps as it rides the AI server boom to a big earnings beat
Broadcom’s stock falls despite upbeat earnings, extending a frustrating stretch for investors
